title: Reduce CPU tail latency with episodic thread groups and marshalling fusion
author: Ethan Kim
description: Motivation: production KPIs show occasional CPU tail spikes driven by request-path serialization and thread pin churn during bursty traffic. Root cause analysis indicated: (1) multiple serializer/deserializer passes over payloads (HTTP->internal frames->task structs), (2) frequent short-lived thread pin/unpin operations when the global workerpool spawns transient workers for bursts, and (3) KV cache fetch misses amplified by per-request scheduling jitter. This PR introduces two complementary changes to reduce per-request CPU overhead and tail latency: (A) Episodic thread groups: lightweight, short-lived groups of workers that are pinned as a cohesive unit to a socket/core subset for the duration of a micro-burst, eliminating repeated pin/unpin syscalls and improving cache locality. Groups are allocated from a small standby allocator with constant-time checkout and returned after an inactivity window. (B) Marshalling fusion: collapse the multi-pass request marshalling pipeline into a single fused pass where possible; the fused path performs framing, header parsing, and payload slicing without copying (zero-copy where backing buffers and lifetimes allow) and defers expensive decoding until after KV cache prefetch signals are resolved. Implementation notes: - Episodic groups are implemented as a thin wrapper over the existing workerpool. We add a GroupLease object (lock-free, sequence-based) and an LRU standby queue keyed by core-affinity mask. Group allocation aims for O(1) latency and supports a fast-fail fallback to the global pool when exhausted. - Marshalling fusion introduces a unified Marshaller object with two codepaths: fused (zero-copy, single-pass) and safe (legacy) mode. Safe mode remains the default unless the request meets a small set of predicates (no custom hooks, payloads are contiguous, no legacy plugin readers). - KV cache prefetch is wire-linked to the fused marshaller: when a fused marshaller sees a cacheable prompt prefix, it emits a prefetch token that the kvcache proactively populates before heavy decode work begins. - Telemetry: added per-request marshalling time, group-hold time, allocator misses, and kvcache-prefetch latency buckets. Rollout strategy: guarded behind runtime feature flag redwood.runtime.episodic_eager and redwood.runtime.fuse_marshalling. Canary rollout: 1% of traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks (p99 latency, error rate, allocator misses). Safety: if group allocation failures exceed threshold or p99 regresses by more than 8%, the flag auto-rolls back for that region. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for GroupLease concurrency and fast-fail path. - Integration tests that validate no-copy lifetimes and fallback correctness under plugin hooks. - End-to-end canary in eu-west-1 with synthetic bursty traffic and real workloads. Benchmarks (canary vs baseline): - Median throughput on m24g: +6% (same model/config) - p50 latency: -5% - p95 latency: -12% - p99 latency: -22% - CPU utilization during bursts: -18% absolute on control-plane core group - KV cache hit latency (tail): -30% Observability changes: dashboard tile for group allocs, marshalling time heatmap, and alert tuned for group allocator miss-rate. Related work: follows up on ENG-1798 (request marshalling refactor) and complements the burst-scheduler work in ENG-1933. Security/privacy: no change to request payload semantics; zero-copy is applied only when buffers are owned or immutable. Migration notes: third-party plugins that inspect raw frames in-place must opt into the fused path via a new PluginCapability flag; otherwise they stay on safe path. See migration doc in docs/runtime/marshalling-fusion.md. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Perf benchmarks - [x] Telemetry added - [x] Canary + rollout plan Commits summary: single-squash with iterative commits during review.

perf(marshalling): implement fused Marshaller zero-copy path with safety predicates
feat(kvcache): introduce prefetch token and async population hook
tests: unit + integration for group leases and marshaller fallbacks
docs: add migration + rollout notes for marshalling fusion
review_comments: Priya Rao: Nice approach. Two questions: how do we ensure group allocation doesn't starve long-running background tasks? Can group leases be preempted?

Ethan Kim: Group leases are non-preemptive for the lease duration but the allocator is sized conservatively; background pools remain backed by the global pool. Added a metric and a circuit to detect starvation and fall back to global pool. See group_lease.cc comments.
Carlos Mendes: The zero-copy path is elegant but I'm worried about plugin compatibility. Can we explicitly gate this behind plugin capability?
Ethan Kim: Yes — fused path is enabled only when PluginCapability::INPLACE_READ is true or when no plugin hooks are present. Added integration test to cover the plugin case.
Lars Becker: CI flaked on the integration test initially (timeout). Re-ran and logs look clean. Please add a synthetic workload benchmark that mimics garbled inputs.
Ethan Kim: Added synthetic fuzz harness and tightened timeouts in the integration test. Re-ran CI.
Priya Rao: Approve after addressing allocator sizing note.
release_notes: Introduce episodic thread groups to reduce pin/unpin overhead and a fused marshalling path that reduces copies and defers decoding until after kvcache prefetch. Improvements target CPU tail latency and throughput during bursts. Backward-compatible safe path and feature flags included.
notes_for_ops: Enable redwood.runtime.episodic_eager and redwood.runtime.fuse_marshalling in canary region with 1% traffic initially. Watch metrics: telemetry.group_alloc_failures, telemetry.marshalling_time.p95, telemetry.request_p99. Auto-rollbacks are configured at >8% p99 regression or allocator-miss-rate > 0.5% for 5m.
